title: Engineering Around Non-Determinism: Evals, Grounding, and Release Gates for AI-Drafted Suspicious Reports
gist: An InfoQ Certified Architect Program capstone proposes a multi-agent, knowledge-graph-grounded architecture for AI-drafted Suspicious Activity Reports, arguing LLM non-determinism must be engineered around with refusal on missing evidence, frozen LLM judges plus deterministic fact-checks, golden-set regression evals, risk-tiered human review and regulated release gates. Architectures are illustrative, not real deployed systems.

insights.claim: Manual Suspicious Activity Report drafting does not scale: quality varies with individual investigators, the process cannot keep pace with rising suspicious-activity volumes, and every case carries a labor cost that is ultimately passed to customers.
insights.speaker: Ritesh Modi
insights.so_what: AML compliance cost is a target for AI automation in banking.

insights.claim: The authors' illustrative example: if 10% of active customers are detected, investigated and reported at $50 of human labor each, compliance meaningfully raises the cost of doing business.
insights.speaker: Ritesh Modi
insights.so_what: Illustrates the per-case economics AI drafting aims to cut.

insights.claim: The proposed design has an agentic system draft the SAR as soon as an investigation closes, shifting human effort from drafting to reviewing and editing to raise throughput and cut cost per case.
insights.speaker: Ritesh Modi
insights.so_what: Compliance workflows are a near-term enterprise use case for agentic AI.
insights.locator: We propose improving the traditional reporting system

insights.claim: The proposed SAR system chains a Data Query Planner, Data Reranker, Drafter, Judge and Coordinator agent, accessing LLMs via a gateway and grounded in a pre-built Event Plot knowledge graph from detection and investigation.
insights.speaker: Ritesh Modi
insights.so_what: Reference architecture for regulated agentic workflows: knowledge graphs + LLM gateways as core components.

insights.claim: A drafting agent should stop with an explicit 'insufficient context' signal when evidence is missing, because a fluent narrative built around gaps is more dangerous than no draft.
insights.speaker: Ritesh Modi
insights.so_what: Refusal-on-missing-data is a key design pattern for AI in regulated domains.
insights.quote: Stopping with an explicit "insufficient context" signal is safer than a fluent narrative built around gaps.

insights.claim: GraphRAG was deliberately not used because the suspect network investigation is already complete, making community detection unnecessary.
insights.speaker: Ritesh Modi
insights.so_what: GraphRAG is not a default; fit depends on whether graph discovery is already done upstream.
insights.locator: Since the investigation of the network is already done

insights.claim: An LLM judge is itself non-deterministic, so its version should be frozen and paired with a deterministic fact-checker for names, dates and amounts.
insights.speaker: Ritesh Modi
insights.so_what: Evaluation tooling combining LLM judges with deterministic checks is a growing need.

insights.claim: Evals act as the test suite for LLM systems — used during development, requirement changes, model updates, ongoing sampling of production spans for drift, and as a gate on every release.
insights.speaker: Ritesh Modi
insights.so_what: Eval platforms become mandatory infrastructure for production AI.

insights.claim: Because models and prompts change, all evals must be re-run against a golden dataset of edge cases before any model upgrade or prompt/config change, with the golden set augmented from human feedback in production.
insights.speaker: Ritesh Modi
insights.so_what: Model upgrades carry regression risk; vendor model churn has a real testing cost for enterprises.
insights.locator: Regression Evals with Golden Data Set

insights.claim: Observability for probabilistic systems must trace the decision trajectory across the LLM itself, RAG retrieval quality and system failures, because non-deterministic degradations rarely cause explicit crashes.
insights.speaker: Ritesh Modi
insights.so_what: AI observability is a distinct product need beyond traditional APM.

insights.claim: Human review remains a policy decision owned by the BSA/AML function, with risk-tiered routing: low-risk familiar typologies get sampled review while novel, high-risk, multilingual or low-confidence cases default to full review.
insights.speaker: Ritesh Modi
insights.so_what: AI in compliance augments rather than replaces accountable officers — limits labor displacement claims.
insights.quote: AI accelerates preparation; it does not replace accountable judgment.

insights.claim: Models and prompts should be treated as regulated production changes: versioned with owners, tested, gated by Engineering, Compliance/AML, Risk and Legal, rolled out via shadow and canary, monitored, and reversible via feature flags.
insights.speaker: Ritesh Modi
insights.so_what: Release governance for AI adds friction and cost — and a tooling market — in regulated industries.

insights.claim: Key production metrics for AI-drafted SARs are factuality pass rate, judge scores, reviewer edit rate, latency, queue age and escalation volume, with automatic fallback to stricter review or full human drafting when thresholds are breached.
insights.speaker: Ritesh Modi
insights.so_what: Reviewer edit rate is a practical KPI for whether AI drafting actually saves cost.
